acceptance: Red test first: replaying the cycle.sealed of 2043, 2046, 2055 emits one selfheal.incident at the third seal, not at the boundary.
At shadow the decision is would_brake and nothing stops; at enforce the brake file is written once.
A task-code FAIL emits no incident.
The stage key is strict with a range and is documented in STE.
Every wave launch arms it (no console step needed).
fix: Subscribe the detector to cycle.sealed with final_verdict FAIL (event-triggered, like inbox curate --event): read the new class recurrence (item failure-class-fingerprint-recurrence) and emit selfheal.incident at once when a pipeline-code class recurs. Add policy healing.live_reaction.stage (off, shadow, enforce; default shadow): at enforce, a T0 or T1 pipeline-code incident with class recurrence >= 2 engages the loop brake and holds the lane items whose files overlap the failing check; at shadow it records would_brake.
notes: Console route: self-heal chain (X12/X13) and the loop brake.
source: console, 2026-10-27, operator: "why did we not find the wave issue at once, why does wave watch not pick up the failed signal and react?" Evidence: cycles 2043, 2046, 2055 (pipeline-code) and 2048 failed on the same build floor defect with 4 different fingerprints and recurrence 0
summary: The X12 incident detector runs only at the wave boundary (evolve boundary run). During wave 144 a pipeline-code FAIL of a known class (cycle 2055, 4th time) emitted only cycle.sealed WARN; no incident, no hold, no brake. The loop kept starting cycles that could hit the same defect.
title: Each sealed FAIL runs the incident detector at once, and a repeating pipeline-code class emits a live incident
